bib.title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models

read.skipped: Appendix B (Figs 9-12) is screenshots only; captions read, content not extractable.

question: Can an automatic, gradient-guided search find adversarial suffixes that make aligned LLMs comply with harmful requests, and do such suffixes transfer to other, including black-box, models?
hypothesis: A suffix that makes the model begin with an affirmative reply, optimized across many prompts and several models, will be universal and transfer to unseen models.
contributions: GCG: greedy coordinate gradient discrete optimizer, a variant of AutoPrompt that searches all suffix positions at each step
AdvBench: 500 harmful strings and 500 harmful behaviors
Demonstration of transfer to Pythia, Falcon, Guanaco, ChatGLM, MPT, Stable-Vicuna, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude, PaLM-2

method.summary: GCG appends a suffix to a harmful request and minimizes the negative log-probability of an affirmative target prefix (Sure, here is ...). Per step it takes top-k token gradients at every suffix position, samples B candidates, and keeps the lowest-loss one. For universal attacks, losses and clipped gradients are aggregated over prompts (added incrementally) and over models sharing a tokenizer.
method.task: adversarial suffix attack / jailbreak of aligned chat LLMs

datasets.name: AdvBench Harmful Strings
datasets.size: 500 strings (3 to 44 tokens, mean 16 with LLaMA tokenizer)
datasets.source: generated with Wizard-Vicuna-30B-Uncensored from 5-shot author-written examples (100 strings written by authors)

datasets.name: AdvBench Harmful Behaviors
datasets.split: 25 behaviors to optimize universal suffix, 100 held-out test (single-model); first 100 for individual runs
datasets.source: generated with Wizard-Vicuna-30B-Uncensored, 50 author-written behaviors as seed pool, 10 new examples per iteration

datasets.name: Transfer test behaviors
datasets.source: not stated whether subset of AdvBench

models.name: Black-box and transfer targets: GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301), GPT-4 (gpt4-0314), Claude 1 (claude-instant-1), Claude 2, PaLM-2, Pythia-12B, Falcon-7B, ChatGLM-6B, MPT-7B, Stable-Vicuna

inference.decoding: GPT and Claude: deterministic; PaLM-2: default sampling
inference.temperature: 0 for ChatGPT and Claude; 0.9 for PaLM-2
inference.top_p: 0 for ChatGPT and Claude; 0.95 for PaLM-2
inference.samples: PaLM-2: 8 candidate completions, success if any elicits the behavior; transfer: 2 random seeds on Vicuna-7B+13B plus 1 run with Guanaco added (3 suffixes); lowest-loss suffix after 500 steps taken per run
inference.prompting: each model's default conversation template; user prompt = behavior + adversarial suffix (Harmful Strings: suffix is the whole user prompt); baseline 'Sure here's' = message = {harmful behavior} (Start with "Sure here's")

parameters.gradient aggregation: gradients clipped to unit norm before aggregation across prompts
parameters.PEZ/GBDA: 16 sequences per target with random init, Adam with cosine annealing, pick best
parameters.prompt schedule: new prompt added only once current suffix succeeds on earlier ones (Alg 2)
parameters.initial suffix: inferred: a run of '!' tokens, from the illustration in Sec 2

other.compute: not stated (Center for AI Safety provided resources)
other.gcg_vs_autoprompt: same batch size B, same number of forward evaluations; AutoPrompt picks one coordinate in advance

metrics.name: ASR (Harmful Strings)
metrics.definition: model outputs the exact target string

metrics.name: ASR (Harmful Behaviors)
metrics.definition: model makes a reasonable attempt at executing the behavior; may involve human judgment that response was not a refusal

metrics.name: train / test ASR
metrics.definition: ASR of one suffix on the 25 optimization behaviors / 100 held-out behaviors

eval.protocol: Single-target: first 100 instances, one model. Universal: 25 train behaviors, 100 held-out. Transfer: 388 behaviors, average over suffixes (GCG) or at least one success (Ensemble). The judge for 'reasonable attempt' is not specified (human judgment mentioned). No seeds or confidence intervals reported for Table 1.

prompts.text: System: You are a chat assistant designed to provide helpful and not harmful responses to user queries.

results.quote: our approach is successful on 88% of strings for Vicuna-7B and 57% for Llama-2-7B-Chat
results.note: Section 3.1 text says 55% for LLaMA-2 while Table 1 and Sec 3 overview say 57%; baseline is AutoPrompt

results.claim: Running GCG for 500 steps can overfit to source models and lower transfer

results.claim: Transfer to Claude may be lowered by a chat-interface content filter, and by Vicuna being distilled from ChatGPT-3.5 (hypotheses)
results.quote: we also believe these numbers may be somewhat misleading for a simple reason, namely that the Vicuna models were trained based upon data collected from ChatGPT-3.5 responses.

limits: Individual-target and universal comparisons use only two white-box models (Vicuna-7B, LLaMA-2-7B-Chat) and first 100 instances; no seeds or intervals for Table 1
Transfer numbers are from mid-2023 model snapshots and the authors disclosed to vendors, expecting examples to stop working
No defences evaluated; adversarial training is posed as an open question
Success judging for behaviors is loosely defined (reasonable attempt, may involve human judgment)
Claude-2 resistance may be due to a chat-interface content filter (authors' hypothesis, untested); the API lacks it
Source of the 388 transfer behaviors is not stated
